description:
FILED s488b (Opus) as the explicit residue of #1841, which shipped the script
cache for a real FILE only.  It is strictly additive: nothing about it changes
what a program does, and the shapes below keep today's transpile-and-load path
until it lands.

WHAT IS NOT CACHED AND WHY (`pcl`, the `$use_script_cache` decision):

  * `pcl -e CODE` / `-E CODE`.  `pcl` writes CODE to a temp .pl whose name is
    fresh every run (File::Temp), so the script key -- which is a PATH key --
    would produce a new entry per invocation and never a hit.  That is not a
    slow cache, it is a LEAK, in the directory family that already has no
    natural ceiling.
  * a FILE run with `-M` prefixes.  `pcl` prepends the `use` lines into a temp
    COPY of the source (so the -M imports are in force) and transpiles that
    copy -- same fresh-name problem, and the copy's content is a function of
    the file plus the -M list.

THE FIX SHAPE: key by CONTENT, exactly as `%p-eval-cache-stem` does for a
string eval -- MD5 over the perl TEXT plus everything else that decides the
emission.  For these two shapes that is: the assembled source text (the -M
prefix lines + the file's bytes, or the -e code), the include path (the same
components #1841's key carries: the -I list, the cwd, PERL5LIB), and the
generation + compiler fingerprint tail every entry carries.  `$0` is `-` for
-e and the real path for the -M-file case, so it is a function of the inputs
already listed.  The entry can live in <cache>/scripts/ beside the path-keyed
ones (the prune, the manifest and the fasl identity are shared) -- a stem is a
stem.

MEASURED PRIZE (s488b, warm core): `pcl -e 1` is 0.165 s, of which ~0.12 s is
the pl2cl process; a cached script of the same size answers in 0.033 s.  So
roughly 0.13 s per invocation for -e, which matters for a loop of one-liners
and not at all for one.  That is why it is a follow-up and not part of #1841.

BAR: rows in Pl/t/script-cache-01.t -- the same text from two different temp
paths is ONE entry (the whole point); two different -M lists over one file are
TWO entries; `pcl -e` twice in a row leaves exactly one entry, not two; and
the -M import-list spelling (`-MFoo=a,b` -> `use Foo ('a','b')`, `-M-Foo` ->
`no Foo`) is part of the keyed text, so each spelling gets its own entry.  The
existing rows that assert "leaves NO script entry" for these two shapes are
the ones that must be REWRITTEN, not deleted -- they encode today's decision.

Related: #1841 (the script cache), #1200 (the string-eval cache this borrows
its keying rule from), #1843/#1861 (the fingerprint tail).
subject: `pcl -e CODE` and a file run with `-M` prefixes are the two shapes the script cache (#1841) does NOT cover: `pcl` writes them to a TEMP source with a fresh random name, so a path-keyed entry would leak one dead entry per run -- key them by CONTENT, the way the string-eval cache keys its texts
